title: Midjourney Pricing in 2026: Plans and Fast Hours
summary: Midjourney pricing includes multiple subscription plans with different monthly costs and generation limits. See the exact price and features for each plan.
body_markdown:
## Track Image Spend with Activepieces


There is no official public API for reading Midjourney usage. Size the plan by what your team actually generates, which means counting it yourself from the Discord channel where its bot posts.


### What can and cannot be automated


Activepieces connects apps through 746 integrations, called pieces, and its MIT-licensed core is free to self-host. It can watch a Discord channel, write rows to Google Sheets and post to Slack.


It can't ask Midjourney how many fast hours remain, and it can't change your plan or stop a job. Anything you build is a tally of what the bot posted, not the balance on your account.


When someone asks why the plan ran dry on Wednesday, that gap matters. A log can show who ran what and when.


It can't show the exact hours the account was charged, so treat it as an early warning and check the real figure on your account page.


### A usage-alert workflow in three steps


Five nodes do three jobs, as listed below: capture the bot's posts (nodes 1 to 3), record them (node 4), and warn someone (node 5). The order matters because each node only works on what the one before it kept.


1. Trigger on new Discord message
2. Filter for Midjourney Bot
3. Extract prompt data
4. Log to Google Sheets
5. Send Slack alert if row count > threshold


Without node 2, chatter inflates your count and the alert fires for no reason, and the team learns to ignore it. The node earns its place by dropping everything people type in that channel.


In node 3, keep the requester's name and the command text, not only the prompt. Video requests cost more than still images, and a row that doesn't say which was which can't explain a sudden spike.


Set the node 5 threshold below the point where work stops, not at it. An alert that arrives after the allowance is gone is only an explanation. Because a row counts jobs and not hours, revisit the number after your first week of real use.


Those five nodes cost one Activepieces credit per run, exactly what a lazy two-node version would cost, because the Activepieces pricing page lists 1 credit per flow run, any number of steps.


Zapier's pricing page bills per task and Make's pricing page bills per module, so on either model the careful filter and the extra extraction step would each add to the bill; here the free plan's 1,000 credits a month and unlimited flows make no such trade.


This is a supporting use, a log and a warning around Midjourney, and it does nothing to fix the plan itself.


Once you have a log, you can compare it against what each plan tier allows.
